publication: The Newark Herald (City Edition, NJ's largest colored weekly)
summary: Vol. 11, No. 22, 12 pages. Front page leads with a US Housing Authority project in Montclair to be occupied by whites and Negroes side by side, and the arrest/guilty plea of Daniel E. Winge, ex-assistant manager of Douglass-Harrison apartments, for embezzlement, plus 'Hoot' Gibson held on mail-robbery charge. Interior pages cover a Mississippi lynching, an NAACP/Elks oratorical contest set for Jersey City July 24, the North Jersey Baptist Association's annual conference at Bethany Baptist Church (Newark), the NJ State Federation of Colored Women's Club convention opening at Bordentown Manual Training School, a profile of Rev. Dr. W. W. Fleming of Mt. Olive Baptist Church (Newark), Newark's Neqron Post of the American Legion, Asbury Park nightlife items, and sports coverage of the Newark Eagles (Negro National League) at Ruppert Stadium and the Viking Tennis Club of Newark/Orange.

incidents.what: US Housing Authority approves Montclair project for joint white and Negro occupancy
Daniel E. Winge arrested and pleads guilty to embezzlement from Douglass-Harrison apartments, Newark; faces sentencing July 20
Mob of white businessmen shoots and kills Tom Green, a 43-year-old Black man, in Rolling Fork, Mississippi -- first recorded lynching of the year
Freehold, NJ man (Joseph Mitchell, 24) killed by blow to head; woman held as suspect
Body of Hackensack woman recovered from Hackensack River
Lightning strikes church gathering in Kingston, NC, killing Asa Woodrow and Ada Harper and injuring others
